title: Cube Root Behavior in the Complex Plane
full_prompt: Write a Manim script (compatible with ManimGL/Manim Community) that visualizes the relationship between a complex number $c$ and its three cube roots $z$ (where $z^3 = c$). Create two complex planes side-by-side: the left plane represents the 'Root Plane' (for $z$) and the right plane represents the 'Coefficient Plane' (for $c$). Place a red dot in the coefficient plane representing $c$, and three yellow dots in the root plane representing the three cube roots of $c$. Animate the coefficient $c$ moving in a complete circle of radius $R$ around the origin in the coefficient plane. As $c$ completes a full $360^\circ$ rotation, show how the three roots in the root plane rotate by $120^\circ$ each, permuting their positions. Use continuous tracers to show the paths of both the coefficient and the roots. Implement a distance-minimizing sorting algorithm (like Hungarian matching or nearest-neighbor sorting) to ensure that the roots update smoothly without discontinuous jumps between frames.

visual_techniques: Dynamic updaters linking root and coefficient positions
Optimal transport/sorting to minimize root jumping

common_failure_modes.note: If roots are not sorted to minimize distance to their previous positions, they will randomly swap identities/colors at branch cuts.
Failing to correctly map complex numbers to the local coordinate systems of the side-by-side planes.
